To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IHC markers are useful in differentiating between prostatic adenocarcioma and benign mimickers.

immunopositivity of 34βE 12 in a discontinous pattern, p63 in a basal cell pattern and immunonegative AMACR are the best immunomarkers to distinguish PAH from low grade prostatic carcinoma (small acinar pattern).
IHC markers are helpful for the differentiation of prostatic adenoma and prostatic adenocarinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of immunohistochemistry in differentiating some benign mimickers from low grade prostatic carcinoma (small acinar pattern).
the use of IHC in the diagnosis of low-grade prostatic carcinoma (small acinar pattern) and its differentiation from PAH, AAH and SAP.
the histological and immunohistological features of prostatic lesions that can mimic low grade prostatic carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
34βE 12 is a useful adjunct in the differential diagnosis of PAH from prostatic adenocarcioma.
IHC is useful for the diagnosis of prostate adenocarcinomas and for differentiating between low grade adenocarcinomata and benign mimickers.

the use of immunohistochemical stains (34βE12, p63 and AMACR) can be contributory in differentiating between low grade prostatic carcinoma (small gland pattern) and some pseudoneoplasms of the prostate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IHC is a very useful tool in the differentiation between low grade prostatic carcinoma and its mimickers, but should be used with care and in conjunction with the H&E morphology.
the use of IHC markers is a helpful adjunctive tool in the diagnosis of low-grade prostatic carcinoma and its differential diagnosis with pseudoneoplastic prostatic lesions.

the use of immunohistochemistry in combination with histopathological examination can help in differentiating between prostatic adenocarcioma and benign mimickers, especially in cases with atypical histology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IHC should always be interpreted in conjunction with morphology.

the use of IHC is not a substitute for the histopathologist’s skill and experience in the interpretation of H&E stained sections, rather it is an adjunctive tool that can be very helpful in the differential diagnosis of prostatic lesions.
34βE-12 can be used as a marker for prostatic adenocarcioma in the absence of p63, but it should be interpreted in light of the H&E findings.
